Atom SDK C++ version — User Guide

Overview

Atom SDK C++ version is a high-performance native SDK for robotics and vision applications, providing type-safe API to drive Atom Server-side graph (Graph) management, node (Node) editing, subgraph node (GraphNode) orchestration, and inference runtime (Runtime) execution capabilities.

Core Features: * High performance: native C++17, no GIL overhead, supports multi-threaded concurrent calls * Type safety: All API are strongly typed, and parameter errors can be caught at compile time * Bundled JSON: the JSON implementation ships with the SDK; no Boost or separately configured JSON library is required * RAII Resource Management: Automatically manage graph resources to avoid leakage * Exception-driven error handling: Unified error reporting through atom::sdk::AtomError and its subclasses The normal JsonObject return value will automatically bring the status field of this request; list, Boolean value, original ByteBuffer, parsed point cloud, bound raw value and node parameter snapshot maintain the original data shape.

Structured parameter naming

The complex interface maintains the same set of parameter object naming as Python SDK: * *Ref: refers to an existing object and is only responsible for locating resources, such as NodeRef, PortRef, BindingRef * *Params: Complete input parameters of an interface call, such as CreateGraphParams, RuntimeRunParams * *Update: Modify existing configurations or values, such as NodeParamUpdate, RuntimeParamsUpdate

auto graph = client.graph().create_graph({"my_graph"});
auto node = client.node().create_node({"my_graph", "ResizeImage"});
// Normal mode example;passive_bino Please use mode RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_file/bytes/images.
auto run_result = client.runtime().run_graph({"my_graph", {frame}});
std::cout << "Run request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

For more information on the field order, file uploading and error-prone points of parameter objects, see 参数对象.

Installation

Prerequisites

  • CMake 3.16+

  • C+17 compatible compiler (GCC 9 / Clang 10+ / MSVC 2019+)

  • System thread library

The SDK does not depend on a system or Conan Boost package. The release includes httplib.h and nlohmann_json.hpp under include/atom_sdk/thirdparty/; consumer projects only need the SDK’s include directory.

First download atom_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center and extract it. No Conan remote or login is required. Inside the archive, cpp/ is split into three platform subdirectories — linux-x86_64, linux-arm64, and windows-x64; the C++ SDK is at <SDK_DIR>/cpp/<platform>/atom_sdk-<version> under whichever one matches your build target.

Step 1: Configure CMakeLists.txt

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(my_project CXX)

# The Windows package only ships a Release build; lock the configuration here.
# You still need to pass --config Release explicitly when building — omitting
# it fails at compile time with MSB8013 instead of crashing at runtime.
if(WIN32)
    set(CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES "Release" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
endif()

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# cpp/ is split into linux-x86_64/linux-arm64/windows-x64 subdirectories;
# auto-select the one matching the current build platform.
if(WIN32)
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "windows-x64")
elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "aarch64|arm64")
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "linux-arm64")
else()
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "linux-x86_64")
endif()
set(ATOM_SDK_ROOT "<SDK_DIR>/cpp/${ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR}/atom_sdk-<version>")

find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

find_library(ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY
    NAMES atom_sdk_cpp
    PATHS "${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/lib"
    NO_DEFAULT_PATH
)

if(NOT ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Cannot find atom_sdk_cpp under ${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/lib")
endif()

add_executable(my_app main.cpp)
target_include_directories(my_app PRIVATE
    "${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/include"
)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE
    "${ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY}"
    Threads::Threads
)

Step 2: Build

# Set ATOM_SDK_ROOT in CMakeLists.txt to the extracted SDK path first
cmake -S . -B build

# --config Release is required on Windows; omitting it fails with MSB8013
cmake --build build --config Release

quick start

The following example shows the minimum usable code for SDK, connecting to the server and listing all graphs:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <cstdint>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

int main() {
    try {
        // Create client,Connect locally Atom service(Default port 10026)
        atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

        // List all images on the server
        atom::sdk::JsonArray graphs = client.graph().list_graphs();

        std::cout << "Current number of pictures:" << graphs.size() << std::endl;

        for (const auto& g : graphs) {
            const auto& obj = g;
            std::string name = obj.at("name").get<std::string>();
            std::cout << "  - " << name << std::endl;
        }

    } catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
        std::cerr << "SDK Error:" << e.what() << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    return 0;
}

Service overview

AtomClient provides 4 subservices, accessed through member methods:

Service Access method Responsibilities

GraphService

client.graph()

Picture creation, deletion, import and export, and entire picture operation

NodeService

client.node()

Add and delete nodes in the main graph, connect them, set parameters, and read ports

GraphNodeService

client.graph_node() Node editing and operation of the internal subgraph of the

subgraph node (GraphNode)

RuntimeService

client.runtime()

Load existing graphs, set parameters, perform inference, and read results

Core type description

C++ type Underlying type Purpose

nlohmann::json (bundled with the SDK)

atom::sdk::JsonObject

JSON object, collection of key-value pairs

nlohmann::json (bundled with the SDK)

atom::sdk::JsonValue

Any JSON value (object/array/string/number/bool/null)

nlohmann::json (bundled with the SDK)

atom::sdk::JsonArray

JSON array

atom::sdk::ByteBuffer

std::vector<uint8_t>

Raw binary data (image/point cloud)

atom::sdk::PortDataResult

structure

port data, including data (JsonObject) and attachments (attachment map)

atom::sdk::SingleNodeResult

std::variant<JsonValue, ByteBuffer>

Single node running result, may be JSON or binary

JSON field access idioms

atom::sdk::JsonObject result = /* ... */;

// Read string field
std::string name = result.at("name").get<std::string>();

// Read floating point number
double score = result.at("score").get<double>();

// Read integer
std::int64_t node_id = result.at("nodeId").get<std::int64_t>();

// Read Boolean value
bool ok = result.at("success").get<bool>();

// Read request status
int status = static_cast<int>(result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>());

// Determine whether the field exists
if (result.contains("optional_field")) {
    // Process when field exists
}

// Read nested objects
const auto& nested = result.at("nested");

// Traverse array
const auto& arr = result.at("items");
for (const auto& item : arr) {
    // item for JsonValue
}

Error handling

All SDK methods throw an atom::sdk::AtomError or its subclass exception on failure, it is recommended to always use the try/catch wrapper:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

try {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    auto result = client.graph().run_graph("my_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
    std::cerr << "Atom SDK Error:" << e.what() << std::endl;
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    std::cerr << "Standard library exception:" << e.what() << std::endl;
}
